title: Shark vs. Roomba: Is either robot vacuum brand worth it now?
excerpt: Shark was ahead after iRobot filed for bankruptcy. Can the newest Roombas spark a redemption arc?
content_html:
Bottom Line

Shark now has a brilliant flagship vacuum that uses UV light to detect stains. That's huge for the brand, even if other models lack detailed mopping and obstacle avoidance. But other than that, Shark's lineup falls flat.

VS

Roomba

Bottom Line

There are more Roomba options with advanced features like small obstacle avoidance tech and corner mopping. But most Roombas are just OK at best, and buying from a company that just went bankrupt feels risky.

Table of Contents

UPDATE: July 25, 2026, 5:00 a.m. ET Five new Roombas were released on July 7, 2026. I'm in the process of testing them at home and will update this comparison guide accordingly.

The conversation surrounding the best robot vacuums in 2026 is a starkly different one than it was in years prior.

In earlier versions of this story, I wrote that the Shark vs. Roomba conversation is the ultimate robot vacuum standoff. But between 2024 and early 2026, the duel between these two household names had turned into a competition of who can be the most mid.

As of July 2026, both brands have finally made some much-needed effort to keep their vacuums relevant. But whether Shark or Roomba is better might still be a moot point. The more realistic question is whether either is even in the running for top robot vacuum brands at all when competitors like Dreame, Roborock, Eufy, and Narwal continue to pump out more dominant robot vacuums.

Nonetheless, Shark and iRobot are still two of the most-searched robot vacuum brands on the internet. I've tested more than 15 models between the two brands, so I have some thoughts on the pros and cons of getting a Roomba or a Shark. For posterity's sake, here's how Shark and Roomba compare in 2026.

Is iRobot out of the bankruptcy hole?

When iRobot filed for bankruptcy in December 2025, the company insisted that a glow-up was in the works — but we didn't know when or if we'd actually see a new Roomba again. Well, it finally happened: In July 2026, iRobot released new Roombas in the U.S. for the first time under its new ownership. But are they smart enough cleaners at practical enough prices to outpace Shark, or serve as real competition with the rest of the best robot vacuum brands?

Let's break down why Roombas were considered the best for so long, where iRobot went wrong, and what the 2026 Roombas are doing to change the "overpriced and underwhelming" narrative.

Where Roomba wins: Small obstacle avoidance and more variety

Shark's family of robot vacuums is definitely growing. But the variety in the Roomba lineup offers slightly more flexibility for mixing and matching staple features like smart mapping, self-empty docks that also wash and dry the mopping pads, automatic cleaning boosts when a mess is detected, and most importantly, small obstacle avoidance technology.

Plus, there are just more Roombas to choose from than there are Shark robovacs. The last two Roomba drops haven't just introduced one or two new Roombas, as is the case with Shark announcements — we're used to getting at least five new Roombas at a time.

The 2025 Roombas all have LiDAR towers — a first for iRobot. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

You can still buy a few of the 2025 Roombas that were released pre-bankruptcy, and they often go on sale. The best Roombas that I've tested recently include the Roomba 105 (a standalone model with smart mapping) that has permanently dropped to $159 and the Roomba Plus 505 Combo (self-washing and -drying mopping pads, small obstacle avoidance) for as low as $499 on sale.

iRobot thankfully diverted from the traditional flat mopping pad with its 2025 overhaul. Now, several mopping Roombas use dual spinning mopping pads — a design that the majority of iRobot customers prefer, iRobot told me in a press briefing. The Roomba Max 705 Combo was actually one of the first mainstream roller mop robot vacuums, which debuted months before that became a major trend at CES 2026. Still, the Max 705 Combo wouldn't be a worthwhile purchase over better roller mop robot vacuums like the Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow or the Eufy C28.

Not for nothing, iRobot heard the cries of the anti-mop crowd on Reddit and answered with a vacuum-only version of one of its more powerful models, the Roomba Max 715 Vac. A lot of people simply don't want to deal with water tanks or anything soggy at all, but finding a vacuum-only robot vacuum typically means settling for a super basic model — all of the most advanced robot vacuums are automatically hybrids nowadays. But since it's completely skipping such a main feature, I think the Roomba Max 715 should be a little cheaper than $699.99.

The Roomba Max 705 Combo has a paint roller-esque mop and a wooden dock. Credit: iRobot

The new Roomba Plus 405 Combo has two spinning mopping pads — a first for iRobot. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

iRobot's widespread application of small obstacle avoidance does provide some leverage over Shark. This staple feature is what keeps the vacuum from eating common floor items like cords, shoes, and toys — and that means less pre-tidying and less babysitting on the human's end.

The cheapest Roomba with front-facing obstacle avoidance cameras, the Roomba Plus 415 Combo, is now just $599.99. Only Shark's top three premium robot vacuums feature small obstacle avoidance cameras, and they're much more expensive than this.

Where iRobot loses: Forgettable vacuums, iffy finances

iRobot isn't exactly the pioneer it once was.

The self-emptying, smart mapping Roomba S9+ of 2019 and the 2021 Roomba j7+ that could avoid cords and pet waste were huge deals when they first hit the scene — they truly set the standard for the rest of the vacuum market. iRobot's star power was so influential that "Roomba" became the colloquial generic term for any robot vacuum.

But somewhere down the line, iRobot stopped innovating in the ways that once justified its steep price points. Roombas started costing way too much for the brainpower or cleaning performance they offered. The Roomba flop era was kind of inevitable.

The Roomba Plus 505 Combo isn't anything special, but it's fine if you find it on sale. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

iRobot has released new Roombas for the first time since filing for bankruptcy and handing ownership to its manufacturer, Picea. I'll give credit to iRobot for getting more practical with its prices, specifically in terms of expanding staple smart features like LiDAR, the self-washing mopping pad system, or small obstacle avoidance to more affordable models. But none of it is anything we haven't seen before.

At this point, iRobot is merely playing catch-up to budget-friendly behemoths like Dreame and Roborock. None of the 2026 Roombas have any overly exciting features that make them stand out in any given price range. Plus, we can't pretend like iRobot's recent financial blunder hasn't soured the trust of customers who heard about the bankruptcy news. Even though things are stable enough to continue manufacturing new products, that doesn't promise that iRobot's finances are in order. After all, iRobot filed for bankruptcy less than a year after releasing eight new Roombas in March of 2025.

Where Shark wins: Spot cleaning and the UV light

Shark robot vacuums haven't exactly been known for their innovation. Historically, it felt like the Sharks were several months to a year late on premium features that all of the other brands had. So the genius packed into the Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 2-in-1 that dropped in March 2026 was a pleasant surprise. The UV Reveal uses a real UV light to detect invisible stains on the floor that a robot vacuum using AI cameras or plain LEDs may not see.

The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 2-in-1. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

One memorable moment from my testing is the UV Reveal finding and mopping up dried cat puke that another premium robot vacuum mop combo didn't thoroughly scrub the week before. It's a game-changing feature for mopping hardwood floors.

In June 2026, Shark had the genius idea to release its two best vacuums in more colors than plain ol' black and white. The Shark UV Reveal is available in four chic earth tones that should better blend in with the room's decor: espresso, evergreen, deep harbor, and ivory. It wouldn't surprise me to hear that the aesthetic color options alone were enough to convince someone to buy a Shark over a Roomba.

The colors of the Shark Luxe collection. Credit: Shark

So yes, the Shark UV Reveal breathed life into an otherwise just OK lineup of Shark robovacs. But for everyone trying to spend less than $1,299.99 on a robot vacuum (or even $949.99, if it's on sale), are the other Shark robot vacuums worth it?

I've always found Shark to be in tune with what the average person is willing to spend on a robot vacuum. The brand consistently offers core capabilities like smart mapping and mopping at affordable price points, topped with a straightforward user experience that doesn't involve a million high-level app functions. It's a particularly enticing brand for first-time robot vacuum owners.

The Shark Matrix RV2310 is a reliable little vacuum. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Shark's approachable price points don't necessarily mean it skimps on cleaning performance, though. Shark Matrix vacuums clean in a grid pattern, approaching the area several times from multiple angles to grab anything it may have missed in the first pass or two. According to Shark, Matrix mode dishes out 30 percent better carpet cleaning than the older RV Shark models. For Shark 2-in-1 robot vacuums, a mop in Matrix mode vibrates 100 times per minute to scrub at stains that likely wouldn't budge from a single pass of a cheaper robot mop or a paper towel. Matrix mopping always comes in clutch for keeping up with the constant layer of shoe prints by my front door.

Shark even extends the Matrix cleaning mechanism to most of its super-affordable models, making any of the RV2310 or RV2300 models a solid choice for a budget robot vacuum. Shark's spot cleaning has been such a streamlined, reliable feature in every Shark robot vacuum I tried. My ultimate spot cleaning test is the area outside either of my cats' litter boxes — even the cheap Shark robot vacuums always got to the right spot and cleared the kitty litter before I walked in there with bare feet.

Every other big brand had at least one model with self-washing and -drying mopping pads far before the Shark PowerDetect Pro series hit the scene in September 2024. They originally cost between $999.99 and $1,199.99, which seemed reasonable (at the time) compared to the models that cost $1,599.99. Both Pro models can now be found on sale for around $699.99.

The Shark PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

For good measure, the PowerDetect models are also equipped with large wheels that hoist the vac over carpet to keep it dry during mopping mode. Those hydraulics put the PowerDetect robot vacuums in the small group of robot vacuums that have never gotten stuck on one of my rug corners or scrambled up my bath mats.

Where Shark loses: Small obstacle avoidance and slow releases

Shark's biggest shortcoming might just be that it takes forever to release new robot vacuums. Brands like Roborock and Dreame seem to drop new crops of robot vacuums twice in the time period that Shark introduces a single new model, making its lineup feel outdated quickly. The typical iRobot release introduces at least three new vacuums at once.

But there are smarter robot vacuums out there for that same $699.99 or less.

Overall, Shark's lineup outside of the UV Reveal feels a little basic compared to its competitors. For instance, the original PowerDetect line was in desperate need of a successor for a while. When Shark did finally "revamp" the series in fall 2025, the upgrades were criminally underwhelming. The major difference is heated mop washing and drying for improved sanitation between mopping sessions, hence "ThermaCharged" in the title. That's not exactly a front-page headline when the vacuum is still so far behind other brands' models in the same price range.

The purple lights indicate "Dirt Detect" mode. Credit: Leah Stodart / Mashable

Another lesser-known late 2025 model, the Shark Stratos NeverTouch robot vacuum, is similarly bland. Its description mentions "ultra-powerful suction" and states that the Stratos delivers twice the suction power of the Roomba i5 Combo. A $799.99 robot vacuum is more powerful than an entry-level Roomba that came out in 2023? Yeah, I would hope so.

Shark is the lone major robot vacuum brand that hasn't really invested in small obstacle avoidance past its fanciest model. Multiple models feature Shark's NeverStuck technology to some degree, but the UV Reveal is the only one I've tested that actually felt like it was really perceiving items lying in front of it. Meanwhile, brands like Eufy, Roborock, Dreame, and now even iRobot have prioritized small obstacle avoidance in robot vacuums at the $500 to $700 range.

The lack of agility around common items like cords, laundry, or pet toys seriously cramps the "premium" feel. This is such a staple feature in my life, as I'm sure it is for anyone whose floor might be cluttered lived in from time to time. In my testing, the Shark ThermaCharged was so inept at diverting obstacles (even large ones) that it gave up on cleaning missions instead of simply driving around a tote bag of groceries or a cordless Dyson vacuum attachment lying on the ground.

In the same vein of too-basic navigation, only the most premium Shark robot vacuums automatically stop mopping when carpet is sensed. This means vacuum and mop mode aren't possible at the same time with any of the 2-in-1 Shark Matrix models, and a person needs to manually attach the water tank to switch to mopping mode. That's enough of a pain to make someone want to skip mopping altogether. Even the cheap Roomba 105 Combo can detect carpet — the first time in recent memory where a base-tier Roomba outshines a base-tier Shark.

For the first time in forever, I think iRobot has stronger cheap robot vacuum options than Shark does. You'd be able to squeeze stronger suction power, better edge mopping, and smarter navigation out of $300 or $400 with a budget Roomba or Roborock vacuum than you would with the $449.99 Shark Navigator or $299.99 Shark IQ, which doesn't even self-empty.

It's the same story on the premium end of the spectrum: UV Reveal aside, the fanciest Sharks cost too much given their skills. They don't necessarily have any glaring flaws, but they're certainly not the most competent or most autonomous robot vacuums you could find for between $500 and $900.

Shark is still locked into a single style of mopping pad

Shark also has yet to grow out of the D-shaped mopping pad, while every other major brand has graduated to dual rotating mops or roller mops. The sonic vibrations of the PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro and PowerDetect ThermaCharged did a solid job of wiping up small spills and shoe stains on my apartment's hardwood, but they weren't able to scrub in corners and along edges as the Roomba 405 or 505 Combo's flexible spinning mops can.

Shark thankfully gave the PowerDetect UV Reveal's mopping pad some mobility. It can slide past the circular body of the vacuum to scrub against flat edges, much like the Roborock Saros 20 Sonic's design. I've personally witnessed the UV Reveal's extending mop pad scrub much closer to walls than other Sharks.

Unfortunately, the UV Reveal's mopping is only geared toward scrubbing dry stains or sticky droplets, not liquid spills. I'm still not 100 percent sold on the D-shaped pad design for that reason, and it's disappointing that Shark locks shoppers into that style of scrubbing. iRobot has branched out to spinning pads and even a roller mop, so people with different mopping needs have more options going with iRobot.

Shark doesn't do itself any favors by refusing to list its vacuums' suction power in Pascals (Pa). Almost every other major robot vacuum brand measures suction power in Pa (even iRobot now), which makes comparing options easy. Shark still insists on keeping an air of mystery by solely comparing suction power to other vacuums in its own family tree, or by making vague claims like "50% better suction than the best-selling iRobot."

Where iRobot and Shark both lose: Their apps suck

Ironically, two of the most longstanding names in the robot vacuum game have the two most outdated-feeling apps. The bare bones home maps in both the Roomba Home and Shark Clean apps are far less intricate than the color-coded maps that Roborock or Eufy offer. Pausing a clean or adding an extra room to the queue is similarly clunky on both.

Our winner: Shark

Neither Shark nor iRobot is in the running to be the best robot vacuum brand overall in 2026. But if you want to pit them against each other for old time's sake, Shark is the more reliable robot vacuum brand.

Revisiting the Shark vs. Roomba debate, my answer is pretty much, "Uh, is there a third option?" It's hard to get enthusiastic when one brand has a singular memorable robot vacuum and the other brand has... none. The Shark UV Reveal 2-in-1 is far more innovative than the latest Roomba 400, 500, and 700 Series Combo models that we have to choose from. Since the rest of the Shark and iRobot lineups are a wash, I think it's safe to give Shark the top spot based on the UV Reveal 2-in-1 alone.

The fact that Shark hasn't gone bankrupt is another bonus point by default, presumably putting it in a more cushioned financial position to keep putting out new products.

However, my mind could change once I'm able to test a majority of the newest Roombas at home.

There are other brands that deserve your attention

Overall, I still think that Dreame vs. Roborock is the new Shark vs. Roomba, and I highly recommend taking a look at all of the Dreame robot vacuums and Roborock robot vacuums within your budget. You're probably going to find an option that's smarter and more powerful than the Roomba and Shark vacuum cleaners in your cart.

How we tested

Seven Shark robot vacuums (the Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 2-in-1, the Shark Matrix Plus 2-in-1, the Shark Detect Pro, the Shark RV2300, the Shark RV2310, the Shark PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro, and the Shark PowerDetect ThermaCharged) and 10 Roombas (the Roomba Plus 405 Combo, the Roomba Plus 505 Combo, Roomba 205 DustCompactor, Roomba 105 Combo, the Roomba j7+, the Roomba Combo j7+, the Roomba Combo j5+, the Roomba Combo j9+, the Roomba 694, the Roomba Combo 2 Essential, and the Roomba Combo 10 Max) were tested on and off for at least two weeks in a 1,500 square foot apartment with both hardwood and tile floors, plus multiple rugs of varying piles.

The Sharks and Roombas in question were all relied on on a daily basis for general upkeep of the whole space as well as spot cleaning. They all tackled identical recurring tasks in rooms like the bathroom, where a litter box lives, or the living room, where hair (both pet and human) and crumbs constantly surface.

For dry vacuuming quality, questions like the following were considered:

  • Is the area visibly cleaner than it was before the robot vacuum came through?

  • Are there corners of the room or edges of the zone that the robot vacuum didn't reach?

  • If I walk in this spot in my bare feet after the robot vacuum has come through, will stuff still be stuck to my feet?

Those that mop tended to shoe prints by the front door, paw prints and minuscule dust by the litter boxes, water spots in the bathroom, and random food or drink stains in the kitchen.

For mopping quality, questions like the following were considered:

  • Can I still see the stains if I look at the area from a different angle?

  • If I shine my Dyson V12 Detect Slim laser on this spot, will tiny pieces of dust still show up?

  • Was this mopping performed with actual cleaning solution, or does this robot vacuum only use water?

For a robot vacuum to be truly worth it, it needs to create an overall hands-off cleaning experience past the technical cleaning itself. Some robot vacuums need so much human intervention that they become more trouble than manual vacuuming. We assessed convenience through the following questions:

  • Does the robot vacuum make it to the designated room or zone without getting sidetracked?

  • Did it bang into the kitchen table legs 10 times or knock over the cat's food bowl while getting to said spot?

  • Is automatic emptying an option?

  • Do I need to spend time tidying the room before sending the robot vacuum out to clean?

Its description mentions "ultra-powerful suction" and states that the Stratos delivers twice the suction power of the Roomba i5 Combo. A $799.99 robot vacuum is more powerful than an entry-level Roomba that came out in 2023? Yeah, I would hope so. Shark is the lone major robot vacuum brand that hasn't really invested in small obstacle avoidance past its fanciest model. Multiple models feature Shark's NeverStuck technology to some degree, but the UV Reveal is the only one I've tested that actually felt like it was really perceiving items lying in front of it. Meanwhile, brands like Eufy, Roborock, Dreame, and now even iRobot have prioritized small obstacle avoidance in robot vacuums at the $500 to $700 range.The lack of agility around common items like cords, laundry, or pet toys seriously cramps the "premium" feel. This is such a staple feature in my life, as I'm sure it is for anyone whose floor might be cluttered lived in from time to time. In my testing, the Shark ThermaCharged was so inept at diverting obstacles (even large ones) that it gave up on cleaning missions instead of simply driving around a tote bag of groceries or a cordless Dyson vacuum attachment lying on the ground. In the same vein of too-basic navigation, only the most premium Shark robot vacuums automatically stop mopping when carpet is sensed. This means vacuum and mop mode aren't possible at the same time with any of the 2-in-1 Shark Matrix models, and a person needs to manually attach the water tank to switch to mopping mode. That's enough of a pain to make someone want to skip mopping altogether. Even the cheap Roomba 105 Combo can detect carpet — the first time in recent memory where a base-tier Roomba outshines a base-tier Shark.For the first time in forever, I think iRobot has stronger cheap robot vacuum options than Shark does. You'd be able to squeeze stronger suction power, better edge mopping, and smarter navigation out of $300 or $400 with a budget Roomba or Roborock vacuum than you would with the $449.99 Shark Navigator or $299.99 Shark IQ, which doesn't even self-empty.It's the same story on the premium end of the spectrum: UV Reveal aside, the fanciest Sharks cost too much given their skills. They don't necessarily have any glaring flaws, but they're certainly not the most competent or most autonomous robot vacuums you could find for between $500 and $900.Shark is still locked into a single style of mopping pad Shark also has yet to grow out of the D-shaped mopping pad, while every other major brand has graduated to dual rotating mops or roller mops. The sonic vibrations of the PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro and PowerDetect ThermaCharged did a solid job of wiping up small spills and shoe stains on my apartment's hardwood, but they weren't able to scrub in corners and along edges as the Roomba 405 or 505 Combo's flexible spinning mops can.Shark thankfully gave the PowerDetect UV Reveal's mopping pad some mobility. It can slide past the circular body of the vacuum to scrub against flat edges, much like the Roborock Saros 20 Sonic's design. I've personally witnessed the UV Reveal's extending mop pad scrub much closer to walls than other Sharks. Unfortunately, the UV Reveal's mopping is only geared toward scrubbing dry stains or sticky droplets, not liquid spills. I'm still not 100 percent sold on the D-shaped pad design for that reason, and it's disappointing that Shark locks shoppers into that style of scrubbing. iRobot has branched out to spinning pads and even a roller mop, so people with different mopping needs have more options going with iRobot. Shark doesn't do itself any favors by refusing to list its vacuums' suction power in Pascals (Pa). Almost every other major robot vacuum brand measures suction power in Pa (even iRobot now), which makes comparing options easy. Shark still insists on keeping an air of mystery by solely comparing suction power to other vacuums in its own family tree, or by making vague claims like "50% better suction than the best-selling iRobot." Where iRobot and Shark both lose: Their apps suckIronically, two of the most longstanding names in the robot vacuum game have the two most outdated-feeling apps. The bare bones home maps in both the Roomba Home and Shark Clean apps are far less intricate than the color-coded maps that Roborock or Eufy offer. Pausing a clean or adding an extra room to the queue is similarly clunky on both.Our winner: SharkNeither Shark nor iRobot is in the running to be the best robot vacuum brand overall in 2026. But if you want to pit them against each other for old time's sake, Shark is the more reliable robot vacuum brand. Revisiting the Shark vs. Roomba debate, my answer is pretty much, "Uh, is there a third option?" It's hard to get enthusiastic when one brand has a singular memorable robot vacuum and the other brand has... none. The Shark UV Reveal 2-in-1 is far more innovative than the latest Roomba 400, 500, and 700 Series Combo models that we have to choose from. Since the rest of the Shark and iRobot lineups are a wash, I think it's safe to give Shark the top spot based on the UV Reveal 2-in-1 alone.The fact that Shark hasn't gone bankrupt is another bonus point by default, presumably putting it in a more cushioned financial position to keep putting out new products.However, my mind could change once I'm able to test a majority of the newest Roombas at home.There are other brands that deserve your attentionOverall, I still think that Dreame vs. Roborock is the new Shark vs. Roomba, and I highly recommend taking a look at all of the Dreame robot vacuums and Roborock robot vacuums within your budget. You're probably going to find an option that's smarter and more powerful than the Roomba and Shark vacuum cleaners in your cart. Credit: Roborock Credit: Dreame Credit: Shark Credit: iRobot How we tested Seven Shark robot vacuums (the Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 2-in-1, the Shark Matrix Plus 2-in-1, the Shark Detect Pro, the Shark RV2300, the Shark RV2310, the Shark PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro, and the Shark PowerDetect ThermaCharged) and 10 Roombas (the Roomba Plus 405 Combo, the Roomba Plus 505 Combo, Roomba 205 DustCompactor, Roomba 105 Combo, the Roomba j7+, the Roomba Combo j7+, the Roomba Combo j5+, the Roomba Combo j9+, the Roomba 694, the Roomba Combo 2 Essential, and the Roomba Combo 10 Max) were tested on and off for at least two weeks in a 1,500 square foot apartment with both hardwood and tile floors, plus multiple rugs of varying piles. The Sharks and Roombas in question were all relied on on a daily basis for general upkeep of the whole space as well as spot cleaning. They all tackled identical recurring tasks in rooms like the bathroom, where a litter box lives, or the living room, where hair (both pet and human) and crumbs constantly surface. For dry vacuuming quality, questions like the following were considered: Is the area visibly cleaner than it was before the robot vacuum came through? Are there corners of the room or edges of the zone that the robot vacuum didn't reach? If I walk in this spot in my bare feet after the robot vacuum has come through, will stuff still be stuck to my feet?Those that mop tended to shoe prints by the front door, paw prints and minuscule dust by the litter boxes, water spots in the bathroom, and random food or drink stains in the kitchen.For mopping quality, questions like the following were considered: Can I still see the stains if I look at the area from a different angle?If I shine my Dyson V12 Detect Slim laser on this spot, will tiny pieces of dust still show up?Was this mopping performed with actual cleaning solution, or does this robot vacuum only use water?For a robot vacuum to be truly worth it, it needs to create an overall hands-off cleaning experience past the technical cleaning itself. Some robot vacuums need so much human intervention that they become more trouble than manual vacuuming. We assessed convenience through the following questions:Does the robot vacuum make it to the designated room or zone without getting sidetracked? Did it bang into the kitchen table legs 10 times or knock over the cat's food bowl while getting to said spot?Is automatic emptying an option?Do I need to spend time tidying the room before sending the robot vacuum out to clean?

围绕 2026 年最好的扫地机器人的讨论与前几年截然不同。

在这个故事的早期版本中，我写道，鲨鱼与 Roomba 的对话是机器人真空吸尘器的终极对峙。 但从2024年到2026年初，这两个家喻户晓的人物之间的对决变成了谁能成为最中锋的竞争。

截至 2026 年 7 月，两个品牌终于做出了一些急需的努力来保持吸尘器的相关性。 但 Shark 还是 Roomba 哪个更好可能仍然是一个有争议的问题。 更现实的问题是，当 Dreame、Roborock、Eufy 和 Narwal 等竞争对手继续推出更具主导地位的扫地机器人时，这两家公司是否还在争夺顶级扫地机器人品牌。

尽管如此，Shark 和 iRobot 仍然是互联网上搜索次数最多的两个扫地机器人品牌。 我已经测试了这两个品牌的超过 15 款型号，因此我对购买 Roomba 或 Shark 的优缺点有一些想法。 为了后代的利益，以下是 2026 年 Shark 和 Roomba 的比较。

iRobot 是否已走出破产困境？

当 iRobot 于 2025 年 12 月申请破产时，该公司坚称发光产品正在进行中，但我们不知道何时或是否会真正再次看到新的 Roomba。 好吧，这件事终于发生了：2026 年 7 月，iRobot 在新的所有权下首次在美国发布了新的 Roombas。 但它们是否足够智能、价格足够实用，足以超越 Shark，或者与其他最好的扫地机器人品牌形成真正的竞争？

让我们来分析一下为什么 Roombas 长期以来被认为是最好的，iRobot 哪里出了问题，以及 2026 Roombas 正在采取哪些措施来改变“价格过高且平淡无奇”的说法。

Roomba 的优势在于：避障小且多样化

Shark 的扫地机器人系列无疑正在不断壮大。 但 Roomba 系列的多样性为混合和匹配主要功能提供了更多的灵活性，例如智能地图、可清洗和干燥拖把垫的自清底座、检测到脏乱时的自动清洁增强功能，以及最重要的小型避障技术。

另外，Robotvacs 的 Roomba 数量比 Shark 的机器人还要多。 最近两次推出的 Roomba 不仅仅推出了一两个新的 Roomba，就像 Shark 发布的情况一样 - 我们习惯于一次至少获得五个新的 Roomba。

2025 年的 Roombas 均配备 LiDAR 塔——这对于 iRobot 来说尚属首次。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

您仍然可以购买一些破产前发布的 2025 年 Roombas，而且它们经常打折。 我最近测试过的最好的 Roomba 包括已永久降至 159 美元的 Roomba 105（带有智能地图功能的独立型号）和低至 499 美元的 Roomba Plus 505 Combo（自动清洗和干燥拖把垫，小型避障）。

值得庆幸的是，iRobot 在 2025 年进行了彻底改造，放弃了传统的平板拖把垫。 iRobot 在新闻发布会上告诉我，现在，一些拖地 Roombas 使用双旋转拖地垫，这是大多数 iRobot 客户更喜欢的设计。 Roomba Max 705 Combo 实际上是首批主流滚轴拖地机器人真空吸尘器之一，它在几个月前首次亮相，成为 2026 年 CES 上的一大趋势。 尽管如此，与 Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow 或 Eufy C28 等更好的滚筒拖把机器人真空吸尘器相比，Max 705 Combo 并不值得购买。

并非没有原因，iRobot 听到了 Reddit 上反对拖把人群的呼声，并推出了其功能更强大的型号之一 Roomba Max 715 Vac 的纯吸尘版本。 很多人根本不想处理水箱或任何潮湿的东西，但找到一个纯真空机器人真空吸尘器通常意味着选择一个超级基本的模型——当今所有最先进的机器人真空吸尘器都是自动混合型。 但由于它完全跳过了这样一个主要功能，我认为 Roomba Max 715 应该比 699.99 美元便宜一点。

Roomba Max 705 Combo 配有一个油漆滚筒式拖把和一个木制底座。 图片来源：iRobot

新款 Roomba Plus 405 Combo 配备两个旋转拖把垫，这在 iRobot 中尚属首次。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

iRobot 在小障碍物回避方面的广泛应用确实为 Shark 提供了一些优势。 这一主要功能可以防止吸尘器吃掉常见的地板物品，如电线、鞋子和玩具，这意味着减少了预先整理工作，也减少了人类的保姆工作。

最便宜的配备前置避障摄像头的 Roomba，Roomba Plus 415 Combo，现仅需 599.99 美元。 只有 Shark 的前三名高级扫地机器人配备了小型避障摄像头，而且它们的价格比这要贵得多。

iRobot 的失败之处：令人遗忘的吸尘器、不稳定的财务状况

iRobot 已不再是以前那样的先驱了。

2019 年的自动排空智能地图 Roomba S9+ 和 2021 年的 Roomba j7+ 可以避免电线和宠物垃圾，它们首次上市时就引起了巨大的关注——它们真正为吸尘器市场的其他产品树立了标准。 iRobot 的明星影响力如此之大，以至于“Roomba”成为任何机器人吸尘器的通俗通用术语。

但后来，iRobot 不再以曾经证明其高昂价格合理的方式进行创新。 Roombas 开始为其提供的脑力或清洁性能花费太多。 Roomba 的失败时代是不可避免的。

Roomba Plus 505 Combo 没什么特别的，但如果你发现它在打折，那就没问题了。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

自申请破产并将所有权移交给制造商 Picea 以来，iRobot 首次发布了新的 Roombas。 我要赞扬 iRobot 在价格上变得更加实用，特别是在扩展主要智能功能（如 LiDAR、自洗拖把垫系统或小型避障功能）方面，使其成为更实惠的型号。 但这些都不是我们以前从未见过的。

目前，iRobot 只是在追赶 Dreame 和 Roborock 等经济型巨头。 2026 Roombas 没有任何一款过于令人兴奋的功能，无法使其在任何给定的价格范围内脱颖而出。 另外，我们不能假装 iRobot 最近的财务失误没有损害听到破产消息的客户的信任。 尽管情况足够稳定，可以继续制造新产品，但这并不能保证 iRobot 的财务状况良好。 毕竟，iRobot 在 2025 年 3 月发布 8 款新 Roombas 后不到一年就申请破产。

Shark 获胜的地方：局部清洁和紫外线

鲨鱼机器人吸尘器并不以其创新而闻名。 从历史上看，鲨鱼在所有其他品牌所拥有的高级功能方面都晚了几个月到一年。 因此，2026 年 3 月推出的 Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 二合一的天才之处令人惊喜。 UV Reveal 使用真正的紫外线来检测地板上的隐形污渍，而使用 AI 摄像头或普通 LED 的扫地机器人可能看不到这些污渍。

Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 二合一。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

我的测试中一个令人难忘的时刻是 UV Reveal 发现并擦拭了另一款高级机器人真空拖把组合在前一周没有彻底擦洗的干猫呕吐物。 这是拖地硬木地板的一项改变游戏规则的功能。

2026 年 6 月，Shark 产生了一个天才的想法，推出了两款最好的吸尘器，其颜色比纯黑色和白色更多。 Shark UV Reveal 有四种别致的大地色可供选择，可以更好地融入房间的装饰：浓缩咖啡色、常青色、深港色和象牙色。 如果听到仅凭美观的颜色选项就足以说服某人购买 Shark 而不是 Roomba，我不会感到惊讶。

Shark Luxe 系列的颜色。 图片来源：鲨鱼

所以，是的，Shark UV Reveal 为原本还不错的 Shark robovacs 系列注入了活力。 但对于每个想花不到 1,299.99 美元购买机器人真空吸尘器的人（甚至 949.99 美元，如果有折扣），其他 Shark 机器人真空吸尘器值得吗？

我一直发现 Shark 与普通人愿意在机器人真空吸尘器上花费的价格相符。 该品牌始终以实惠的价格提供智能地图和拖地等核心功能，并提供简单的用户体验，不涉及数百万个高级应用程序功能。 对于初次使用扫地机器人的用户来说，这是一个特别有吸引力的品牌。

Shark Matrix RV2310 是一款可靠的小型真空吸尘器。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

不过，Shark 平易近人的价格并不一定意味着它在清洁性能上有所欠缺。 Shark Matrix 真空吸尘器以网格模式进行清洁，从多个角度多次接近该区域，以抓住在第一遍或第二遍中可能错过的任何东西。 据 Shark 称，Matrix 模式的地毯清洁效果比旧款 RV Shark 型号好 30%。 对于 Shark 二合一扫地机器人，Matrix 模式下的拖把每分钟振动 100 次，可擦洗较便宜的机器人拖把或纸巾一次擦过后可能无法去除的污渍。 矩阵拖把总是紧随其后，以跟上我前门不断的鞋印层。

Shark 甚至将 Matrix 清洁机制扩展到其大多数超实惠型号，使 RV2310 或 RV2300 型号成为经济型扫地机器人的可靠选择。 在我尝试过的每台 Shark 扫地机器人中，Shark 的定点清洁功能都是如此精简、可靠。 我的最终现场清洁测试是我的猫的猫砂盆外面的区域 - 即使是便宜的 Shark 机器人真空吸尘器也总是能到达正确的位置并在我赤脚走进那里之前清理猫砂。

早在 Shark PowerDetect Pro 系列于 2024 年 9 月上市之前，其他每个大品牌都至少有一款带有自动清洗和干燥拖把垫的型号。 它们最初的价格在 999.99 美元到 1,199.99 美元之间，与售价 1,599.99 美元的型号相比，这在当时看来是合理的。 两款 Pro 型号现已发售，售价约为 699.99 美元。

Shark PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

为了更好地衡量，PowerDetect 型号还配备了大轮子，可将吸尘器提升到地毯上，以在拖地模式下保持干燥。 这些液压系统将 PowerDetect 机器人真空吸尘器置于一小群机器人真空吸尘器中，这些机器人真空吸尘器从未卡在我的地毯角或爬上我的浴室垫。

Shark 的劣势：小障碍物躲避和缓慢释放

Shark最大的缺点可能就是它需要很长时间才能发布新的机器人吸尘器。 在 Shark 推出一款新型号的期间，Roborock 和 Dreame 等品牌似乎两次推出新的扫地机器人产品，使其产品线很快就过时了。 典型的 iRobot 版本会同时引入至少三个新的真空吸尘器。

但市面上还有更智能的扫地机器人，价格同样为 699.99 美元或更低。

总体而言，与竞争对手相比，Shark 在 UV Reveal 之外的阵容感觉有点简单。 例如，最初的 PowerDetect 系列一度急需继任者。 当《Shark》最终在 2025 年秋季“改造”该系列时，升级却非常平淡。 主要区别在于加热拖把清洗和干燥，以改善拖地期间的卫生状况，因此标题中为“ThermaCharged”。 当真空吸尘器仍然远远落后于相同价格范围内其他品牌的型号时，这并不是一个头版头条新闻。

紫色指示灯表示“污垢检测”模式。 图片来源：Leah Stodart / Mashable

另一款鲜为人知的 2025 年末型号 Shark Stratos NeverTouch 扫地机器人也同样平淡无奇。 它的描述提到了“超强吸力”，并指出 Stratos 的吸力是 Roomba i5 Combo 的两倍。 799.99 美元的扫地机器人比 2023 年推出的入门级 Roomba 更强大？ 是的，我希望如此。

Shark 是唯一一个在其最奇特的型号之后还没有真正投资于小型避障机器人的主要品牌。 多个型号在某种程度上都采用了 Shark 的 NeverStuck 技术，但 UV Reveal 是我测试过的唯一一款真正感觉它能感知到前面的物体的型号。 与此同时，Eufy、Roborock、Dreame 等品牌，甚至现在的 iRobot 都优先考虑在 500 至 700 美元范围内的机器人真空吸尘器中实现小型避障。

电线、衣物或宠物玩具等常见物品缺乏灵活性，严重限制了“高级”感觉。 这是我生活中的一个主要功能，因为我相信对于那些地板可能不时杂乱的人来说也是如此。 在我的测试中，Shark ThermaCharged 在转移障碍物（甚至是大障碍物）方面非常无能，以至于它放弃了清洁任务，而不是简单地驾驶着装满杂货的手提袋或躺在地上的无绳戴森真空附件。

与过于基本的导航相同，只有最优质的 Shark 机器人真空吸尘器在检测到地毯时会自动停止拖地。 这意味着任何二合一 Shark Matrix 型号都无法同时进行吸尘和拖地模式，并且需要手动连接水箱才能切换到拖地模式。 这足以让人想完全不擦拖地了。 即使是便宜的 Roomba 105 Combo 也能检测到地毯——这是最近记忆中低端 Roomba 首次胜过低端 Shark。

我认为 iRobot 有史以来第一次比 Shark 拥有更强大的廉价机器人吸尘器选择。 与售价 449.99 美元的 Shark Navigator 或 299.99 美元的 Shark IQ 相比，你花 300 或 400 美元就能获得更强的吸力、更好的边缘拖地功能和更智能的导航功能，后者甚至不能自动清空。

对于高端产品来说，情况也是如此：除了紫外线显示之外，考虑到它们的技能，最华丽的鲨鱼的成本太高了。 它们不一定有任何明显的缺陷，但它们肯定不是你能找到的 500 至 900 美元之间最有能力或最自主的机器人吸尘器。

Shark仍被锁定在单一款式的拖布垫上

Shark 还没有摆脱 D 形拖把垫的束缚，而其他主要品牌都已经升级到双旋转拖把或滚筒拖把。 PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro 和 PowerDetect ThermaCharged 的​​声波振动可以很好地擦拭我公寓硬木上的小溢出物和鞋渍，但它们无法像 Roomba 405 或 505 Combo 的灵活旋转拖把那样擦洗角落和边缘。

值得庆幸的是，Shark 为 PowerDetect UV Reveal 的拖把垫提供了一些移动性。 它可以滑过真空吸尘器的圆形主体，擦洗平坦的边缘，很像 Roborock Saros 20 Sonic 的设计。 我亲眼目睹了 UV Reveal 的延伸拖把垫比其他 Shark 更靠近墙壁擦洗。

不幸的是，UV Reveal 的拖地功能仅适用于擦洗干污渍或粘性液滴，而不是液体溢出物。 由于这个原因，我仍然没有 100% 接受 D 形垫设计，而且令人失望的是 Shark 将购物者锁定在这种擦洗方式中。 iRobot 已扩展到旋转垫甚至滚筒拖把，因此具有不同拖地需求的人可以在 iRobot 上有更多选择。

Shark 拒绝以帕斯卡 (Pa) 为单位列出吸尘器的吸力，这对自己没有任何好处。 几乎所有其他主要扫地机器人品牌都会以 Pa 为单位测量吸力（现在甚至包括 iRobot），这使得比较选项变得很容易。 Shark 仍然坚持保持神秘气氛，仅将吸力与自家家族中的其他吸尘器进行比较，或者做出模糊的声明，例如“比最畅销的 iRobot 吸力强 50%”。

iRobot 和 Shark 都失败的地方：他们的应用程序很糟糕

讽刺的是，机器人吸尘器游戏中最古老的两个名字却拥有两个最过时的应用程序。 Roomba Home 和 Shark Clean 应用程序中的基本主页地图远没有 Roborock 或 Eufy 提供的颜色编码地图那么复杂。 暂停清理或在队列中添加额外的空间对于两者来说同样笨重。

我们的获胜者：鲨鱼

Shark 和 iRobot 都没有有望成为 2026 年最佳扫地机器人品牌。 但如果你想让它们互相竞争，Shark 是更可靠的机器人吸尘器品牌。

重新审视 Shark 与 Roomba 的争论，我的回答几乎是，“呃，还有第三种选择吗？” 当一个品牌拥有一款令人难忘的机器人吸尘器，而另一个品牌却拥有……时，很难让人感到热情。 没有任何。 Shark UV Reveal 二合一比我们必须选择的最新 Roomba 400、500 和 700 系列组合型号更具创新性。 由于 Shark 和 iRobot 系列的其余产品都比较弱，我认为仅凭 UV Reveal 2 合 1 就可以让 Shark 占据榜首。

Shark 没有破产这一事实是默认的另一个加分项，这可能使它的财务状况更加有缓冲，可以继续推出新产品。

我们如何测试

7 个 Shark 扫地机器人（Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal 2 合 1、Shark Matrix Plus 2 合 1、Shark Detect Pro、Shark RV2300、Shark RV2310、Shark PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro 和 Shark PowerDetect ThermaCharged）和 10 个 Roombas（Roomba Plus 405 Combo、Roomba Plus 505 Combo、Roomba 205） DustCompactor、Roomba 105 Combo、Roomba j7+、Roomba Combo j7+、Roomba Combo j5+、Roomba Combo j9+、Roomba 694、Roomba Combo 2 Essential 和 Roomba Combo 10 Max）在一间 1,500 平方英尺的公寓中进行了至少两周的断断续续的测试，该公寓铺有硬木地板和瓷砖地板，并配有多块不同绒头的地毯。

每天都依赖 Sharks 和 Roombas 来进行整个空间的一般维护以及现场清洁。 他们都在房间里处理相同的重复任务，比如浴室，那里有一个垃圾箱，或者客厅，那里的头发（包括宠物和人类）和面包屑不断浮出水面。

对于干式真空吸尘质量，考虑了以下问题：

  • 该区域是否明显比机器人真空吸尘器通过之前更干净？
  • 是否存在机器人吸尘器未到达的房间角落或区域边缘？
  • 如果我在机器人吸尘器通过后赤脚走在这个地方，东西还会粘在我的脚上吗？

那些拖地的人往往会清理前门的鞋印、垃圾箱的爪印和微小的灰尘、浴室的水渍以及厨房里随意的食物或饮料污渍。

对于拖地质量，考虑了以下问题：

  • 如果我从不同的角度观察该区域，我还能看到污渍吗？
  • 如果我用 Dyson V12 Detect Slim 激光照射这个地方，还会出现微小的灰尘吗？
  • 这个拖地是用实际的清洁溶液进行的，还是这个机器人真空吸尘器只用水？

要想让机器人吸尘器真正物有所值，它需要创造一种超越技术清洁本身的全面的不干涉清洁体验。 有些机器人吸尘器需要大量的人工干预，以至于它们比手动吸尘器更麻烦。 我们通过以下问题评估便利性：

  • 扫地机器人是否能够顺利到达指定的房间或区域而不会偏离轨道？
  • 它在到达上述地点时是否撞到了厨房的桌腿 10 次，或者撞翻了猫的食盆？
  • 可以选择自动清空吗？
  • 在将扫地机器人送去清洁之前，我需要花时间整理房间吗？
